A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MindForge and provide readable main text, figures, tables and appendices. The changed title, layout and appendix organization do not prevent matching the method and experiments.

before.justification: v3 reports original Minecraft experiments, including task-completion rates, human/expert interactions, communication ablations, OOD transfer and tech-tree progression.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds component ablations, expert-primed peer-interaction experiments and further reported comparisons.

M1.justification: The BigToM/BDI representation, perspective-taking, failure-triggered communication and three memory subsystems are retained. The new prompts and retrieval specifications document existing components; the PDFs do not establish an underlying algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Minecraft dirt/wood collection, tech-tree progression, post-collaboration/OOD transfer, and execution-log/wiki fine-tuning data. The OOD experiment moves from v3 Section 5.4/Table 3 to v4 Appendix A/Table 4. Added experiments vary agents, components and communication within this retained coverage; MineCollab is only discussed.

E2.justification: The tech-tree comparison expands substantially: v4 Table 3 adds GPT-4-powered ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT alongside the Voyager and MindForge variants retained from v3 Table 4. These methods have reported result rows, rather than merely new citations.

E3.justification: v4 adds longer expert-guided communication schedules, a multi-stage experiment pairing previously GPT-4-instructed Mixtral agents, and Llama 3.1-70B expert configurations. These expand the evaluation design. The exact priming and round accounting remain inconsistent between Section 1 and Section 5.5/Figure 6; the newly specified four-action base setup alone does not establish that the existing experiments changed.

E4.justification: v4 adds direct perspective-taking removal experiments across communication rounds (Appendix B/Table 5) and episodic-memory removal experiments across models and tasks (Appendix C/Table 6). It also extends the communication analysis to longer instructive exchanges and expert-primed peer interactions. These substantially strengthen component-level investigation beyond v3's communication-round and non-collaborative ablations.

E5.justification: v4 Figure 1 newly specifies that its curves are averaged across three runs. Both versions already report 24 independent task trials and three-trial tech-tree averages with ± values. This is a limited reporting clarification, without evidence of increased runs or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v4 adds baseline, alternative-expert, component-ablation and extended communication results; Table 5, for example, reports 67% versus 54% success with versus without perspective-taking after three rounds. Retained tech-tree and OOD scores are unchanged. Numerical inconsistencies also appear: the reported average human-expert gain changes from 49.83% to 57.85% despite equivalent underlying rates, and the two-round Mixtral point changes from 61% to 62% while v4 Table 5 retains 61%.

T1.justification: The causal representations and BDI concepts are retained without new formal definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs. v4 invokes the Condorcet Jury Theorem as an interpretive analogy, without a formal theorem application or mathematical argument.

C1.justification: v4 foregrounds successful matched-expertise learning after expert priming, extending v3's emphasis on expert-assisted improvement and unsuccessful weak-peer collaboration. It introduces social-distillation and test-time-scaling claims. The abstract also explicitly locates the retained 2.3× item and 3× milestone gains in a GPT-4-assisted instructive setting.

C2.justification: v3's expert-dependence interpretation is qualified by v4's account of priming, competence thresholds and communication-induced collective improvement. New appendices explain perspective-taking through more targeted advice and argue for episodic-memory benefits, although Table 6 shows mixed effects. v4 also removes the explicit limitation concerning evaluation only in Minecraft.

D1.justification: v4 supplies previously missing perspective-taking and belief-update prompts, per-belief LLM-call details, and episodic-memory retrieval specifications: text-embedding-ada-002, five retrieved failure episodes and LLM summarization. It clarifies action scheduling and memory updates. API-provider and fine-tuning disclosures are largely retained after relocation, while v3's supplementary-code access statement disappears.

R1.justification: v4 adds targeted references and connections to Hinton's distillation, Snell et al.'s test-time compute scaling, Austen-Smith and Banks's Condorcet analysis, and White et al.'s MineCollab work. Most literature and the core positioning as a Voyager extension using BigToM, BDI and cognitive memory remain intact.

P1.justification: The title changes from collaborative to cultural learning, and the abstract, introduction, related-work passages and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around instructive and matched-expertise learning, OOD material moves to the appendix, and the appendices are extensively restructured around components, prompts and implementation.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the two-column main layout with a single-column format, moves Figure 1 to the opening page, merges v3 Figures 4–5 into a two-panel failure-correction figure, and relocates the belief diagram. Table 2 changes from absolute rates to mostly deltas; expanded plots, two ablation tables, a communication-flow diagram and additional prompt boxes substantially alter the displays.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies previously missing component ablations and concrete prompt/retrieval details, improving scrutiny and reproducibility. However, its new central peer-learning claim has conflicting expert-seeding and round descriptions in Section 1 versus Section 5.5/Figure 6; expert-gain summaries disagree with Table 2, and the memory-benefit interpretation exceeds Table 6. These substantive benefits and new weaknesses in claim-to-result consistency leave the net quality change uncertain.
